title_en: Document layer scheme, A through D
note_en: The opaque letter layers of the old corpus, replaced by six named layers (canon, spec, research, ops, plan, release) that say what a document is rather than how finished it is.

title_en: The account backend
note_en: One process holding sessions, newsletter, keys, connectors, billing, teams, the graph proxy and the community API, reached at /api on the site's own origin so the session cookie stays host-only and every request is first-party.

title_en: Registry-side image builds
note_en: Server images are built by the container registry's build service, which parses the image definition with its own parser and does not deliver heredoc bodies, so a green build can produce an artifact that is missing a third of itself.

title_en: Answer material
note_en: Whether a read actually returns a sentence worth quoting: the node context call projects a one-liner column that no write path fills, while the material the concepts do carry sits in props.note and is not projected.

title_en: Ask, a conversational surface with no language model
note_en: An intent router and answer assembly built on retrieval alone, which degrades to search results or asks back rather than filling an empty answer.

title_en: Atlas, the map surface
note_en: The first screen, called Home on screen and atlas in every identifier, the only surface that registers handles with the shell and the only one that owns the map controls in the top bar.

title_en: Cloud infrastructure, one resource group
note_en: Containers on a consumption environment, a managed relational database and a static web app with a linked backend, adopted because the subscription refused compute provisioning in every region tried.

title_en: Payment processor abstraction
note_en: Payment starts with one merchant of record, with a domestic processor added later if growth warrants, and Vinc never sees or stores card data.

title_en: Continuous delivery on federated credentials
note_en: Deployment authenticates with federated credentials and no long-lived secret, through one application registration carrying one credential per repository, with the role assignment scoped to the resource group rather than the subscription.

title_en: Chunk is the source of truth for document text
note_en: Source text exists only as offset-joined chunk text inside the graph, with no document blob column and no reference to an original file, so the source of truth survives the file being deleted.

title_en: The community pack gallery
note_en: A member publishes a knowledge pack to a public gallery that anyone can read and download, and a signed-in member can import one straight into their own hosted graph.

title_en: The copy deck is canonical
note_en: The deck compiled into the binary and the browser bundle decides what a user reads, and the specification is the rule set and the audit view, because the two previously named each other as the source of truth and so neither was.

title_en: Five delivery surfaces
note_en: The desktop application, the static site with web Vinc, the account backend, the hub with its sidecar and MCP server, and the database, of which only the last is still applied by hand.

title_en: The desktop release pipeline
note_en: A three-platform matrix builds a frozen Python sidecar and a desktop bundle into a draft release, and a person presses publish.

title_en: The topic ceiling on the free tier
note_en: Free is limited by five topics rather than by calls, exceeding it blocks creating a new topic and nothing else, and enforcement lives at the point a topic is created rather than on the screen offering the button.

title_en: The multilingual embedding model
note_en: A multilingual model replaced the English-only one, which had no Korean syllable tokens at all, and the deployed artifact is a self-built int8 with range reduction rather than the vendor build.

title_en: Platform authentication on the linked backend
note_en: Linking the account container as the static web app's backend switches on the platform's built-in authentication automatically, which cut the hub's call to the account's internal verification path before it reached the application.

title_en: Mutual trust on public keys alone
note_en: The account backend and the hub never read each other's database and share no secret; each pins only the other's verification key, which is invariant B2 and adr-security-102.

title_en: The embedding worker
note_en: A background worker fills empty chunk vectors on a timer, dropping the vector index before the fill and rebuilding after, because writing a vector where there was none is an index insertion and that kills the process rather than raising.

title_en: Fail-open degradation
note_en: A check that stays permissive when it cannot decide: the plan refresh keeps the last known value when the account lookup fails, an assertion with no plan claim gets no ceiling at all, and quotas gate the connector route only while the web path runs unmetered.

title_en: Fragment merge, the one write path
note_en: Merges on exact id match only and makes no similarity judgment, routes user-authored types into the general Entity carrier rather than skipping them, and stamps a revision only when a tracked field actually differs.

title_en: The previous provider's infrastructure, deleted
note_en: A single virtual machine with a reverse proxy, service units and a managed database, deleted outright on 2026-07-28 and 2026-07-29, so any description of it is history rather than this system.

title_en: GRAPH.md, the assistant writing conventions contract
note_en: One page of markdown an assistant reads before it writes to the graph, filling the one read channel that MCP left empty.

title_en: The hub, the hosted data plane
note_en: One container running the sidecar and the MCP server over a single embedded store on a mounted file share, pinned to exactly one replica because the store admits one writer.

title_en: Hybrid retrieval, keyword and vector
note_en: A query runs a vector arm and a keyword arm and the two ranked lists are fused by a pure function outside the backend with the query embedding injected, which is what keeps the search path model agnostic.

title_en: In-process state on the account backend
note_en: Rate limit counters, the purge schedule and the release mail ceiling all live inside one process, so the limits hold only while the application stays pinned to a single replica.

title_en: Blocking the internal paths at the edge
note_en: The previous reverse proxy refused the internal paths at the door, that layer disappeared with the provider and no ingress rule replaced it, so one signature check now stands in front of owner-forced reads and writes and a whole-account deletion route.

title_en: LadybugDB, the embedded driver
note_en: The single embedded graph driver, reached through one unconditional import, and when it is absent the store degrades to unreachable with the reason on the health route rather than crashing.

title_en: The document tree in the left column
note_en: adr-design-069 put a tree in the left column that marks the active topic and document continuously, which is why the breadcrumb was removed and back became a key rather than a target.

title_en: The authorization gate for the remote profile
note_en: Protected-resource and authorization-server metadata, dynamic client registration and authorization codes with proof-key exchange, implementing the specification and nothing vendor specific, which is why two different browser assistants register against the same gate.

title_en: Member API keys
note_en: A member mints a key on the site whose plaintext is shown once and is stored only as a keyed hash, and the hub verifies a presented key by asking the account over the internal route.

title_en: The mention linker
note_en: MENTIONS links a chunk to the concepts it names, which is what lets search return the sentence behind a concept, and relinking runs after a document write so a new concept immediately joins the view and search graph.

title_en: Newsletter subscription and delivery
note_en: Double opt-in subscription whose only truth is one confirmed row keyed by address, with unsubscribe that needs no session and never reveals whether an address was subscribed.

title_en: The observability gap
note_en: The only alerting is the spend budget, so every incident in this project has been discovered by a user report or by chance rather than by a check.

title_en: The open layer, carried by Entity and TYPED
note_en: A user-authored type is carried as a value inside the fixed columns of an Entity node and a TYPED relation, and the layer was ported into the live write path rather than revived as its own engine so it inherits revision stamping, owner isolation and deduplication.

title_en: Owner isolation
note_en: Scope filters apply as a pre-filter on the search path and not only on traversal, the owner is forced from a signed subject rather than accepted from a request, and zero out-of-scope rows is a gate condition rather than a goal.

title_en: Parent and child vectors
note_en: The chunk stays at two thousand characters and carries several vectors, one per piece of at most five hundred tokens, and a hit on a child returns the parent, which equals re-chunking exactly while keeping concept links, excerpts and topic derivation at baseline.

title_en: Plan entitlement: free, pro, and team
note_en: One source of truth for a person's entitlement, reaching the enforcement points by three routes that must all agree, because a discrepancy between them is invisible to the user.

title_en: The graph proxy allowlist, registered in three places
note_en: An operation reaches the browser only if it appears in the sidecar routes, the hub proxy operation map and the account read or write map, and missing one kills that feature quietly on the web alone.

title_en: Owner purge on account deletion
note_en: A purge routine detach-deletes every owner-scoped label plus that owner's tombstone table, reachable remotely only behind a signed request from the account, and it is attempted before the account rows are removed so a failure stops the deletion rather than orphaning a graph.

title_en: Token purpose confusion
note_en: Neither the peek nor the consume helper constrains a magic-link token's purpose, so a team invitation or a deletion confirmation link submitted to the verification route yields a session for the address it names.

title_en: The call quota
note_en: Two thousand tool calls a day, identical across all three tiers and held as an environment value rather than a code constant, enforced server side when the hub resolves authorization.

title_en: v0.7.2, a bundle of three planned streams
note_en: Account policy, retrieval and conventions work, and a stream declared empty by reading the commit range, bundled into one release that shipped on 2026-08-03 carrying a fourth stream the plan never mentioned.

title_en: The totals view, a three-column Sankey
note_en: Source, then topic, then connection state, where every column must sum to the same total, so a column that does not balance means the classification is not a partition.

title_en: The store schema version
note_en: Migration applies the base declaration idempotently, then the alterations recorded past the stored version, then records the new one. The version is eight.

title_en: The Signal design system
note_en: The application's design language, dark first with a periwinkle indigo accent and state carried by notation alongside color. The Figma variable collections that carried its name were deleted in the 2026-08-06 rebuild and replaced by primitive and semantic collections, while the token names in the shipped stylesheet still read Signal.

title_en: Silent configuration failure
note_en: A misconfiguration that starts cleanly and answers health with two hundred while one feature is dead, which is the shape of the missing issuer, the missing internal address and the blocked member keys.

title_en: Single writer
note_en: Writes serialize through one job-queue worker, and this is a correctness rule rather than a performance preference: one write issued on a query connection refuses every ordinary merge from the worker for its duration.

title_en: The surface tree
note_en: adr-design-015 established five surfaces and a Settings popover; three surfaces route today and Settings is a modal over whichever one is open, so the five-surface tree no longer exists.

title_en: Three-way field merge on synchronization
note_en: Local and account graphs converge bidirectionally through export, apply and an orchestrator that carries only what changed since last time, over a deliberately narrow set of fields a fragment can round-trip.

title_en: A team graph is one owner string
note_en: The graph engine has no concept of a team: a team graph is the owner column holding an opaque string with a different prefix, which is why the whole feature needs no schema change.

title_en: Team roles: viewer, editor, admin
note_en: Permissions are per operation rather than per node, enforced at the hub and again at the account proxy, with a drift test requiring the union of the role table to equal the full proxy allowlist.

title_en: The user-authored type vocabulary
note_en: Node and edge type is a vocabulary the user authors, one per theme, living outside the graph as a sibling file of the database, where the system may propose and only the user ratifies.

title_en: Two time bases: recorded and content
note_en: adr-design-072 split the axis into when the row was written and the time the document is about, with content time a free string compared lexicographically and never parsed.

title_en: The updater signing key
note_en: A key pair belonging to the application framework signs the update manifest and proves a bundle is the one we published, which is a different thing from operating system code signing and removes no first-run warning.

title_en: Version pin discipline
note_en: The embedded driver version is pinned in the integration workflow, the hub deployment workflow, the release workflow and the hub image definition, and missing one quietly ships something else.

title_en: Connector approval
note_en: The hub sends a signed request assertion, the account verifies it and shows the consent screen using verified values rather than anything the client claimed, and on approval issues its own short single-use assertion.

title_en: The Vinc MCP server
note_en: The package is named vinc_mcp so it cannot shadow the official SDK, its tool registry is the authority for the tool list, and its only downstream surface is an HTTP client for the sidecar.

title_en: Share Pack, the vincpack format
note_en: The account-to-account transfer format whose body is the same nodes and edges shape the ingestion tool accepts, so importing reuses fragment merge as is. It became a zip container in adr-engineering-055, reading accepts both shapes and only writing produces a zip, and preference signals are structurally absent.

title_en: The vincs.io domain
note_en: The canonical domain, an apex and two subdomains on managed certificates, with the older zone kept for outbound mail records only.

title_en: Web Vinc, the browser build
note_en: The same frontend bundle as the desktop app with its data base path pointed at the account instead of a local sidecar, authenticated by the account session and at full write parity.

title_en: Delivery pipeline junction
note_en: Joins the hub, the five delivery surfaces, continuous delivery on federated credentials and the desktop release pipeline.

title_en: Domain migration junction
note_en: Joins the account backend, the cloud infrastructure and the vincs.io domain.

title_en: Embedding pipeline junction
note_en: Joins the hub, the embedding worker and the multilingual embedding model.

title_en: GRAPH.md junction
note_en: Joins chunk as the source of truth for document text, the GRAPH.md conventions contract, the Vinc MCP server and the decision registry.

title_en: Member key junction
note_en: Joins member API keys, the call quota, the authorization gate for the remote profile and the account backend.

title_en: Proxy allowlist junction
note_en: Joins web Vinc, the hub, owner isolation and the graph proxy allowlist.

title_en: First deployment of the account backend on the previous provider
note_en: The account backend and the site first went live on a single hardened virtual machine behind a reverse proxy at the previous provider, the substrate that was deleted outright two weeks later.

title_en: Cross-owner reads on the hosted graph
note_en: Hosted reads could return another owner's rows, which turned owner isolation into a scope filter forced onto every read path rather than an assumption, registered as adr-security-001.

title_en: v0.2.0, member connector onboarding and tier quotas
note_en: The release that ended pasting an administrative key into every connector: a signed-in member approves the connection on the site, the hosted graph is separated per member, and a daily call ceiling arrives.

title_en: The community pack gallery went live
note_en: Publishing a pack to a public gallery shipped on the web Packs surface behind a consent gate, with the owner forced from the session rather than taken from the payload.

title_en: Account deletion made to purge the hosted graph
note_en: Deleting an account began detach-deleting that owner's graph through a signed internal request, attempted before the account rows are removed so a failure stops the deletion rather than orphaning a graph.

title_en: The write path closed to cross-tenant writes
note_en: Delete, merge, pin, tag and ingest gained an owner predicate and the remote call began overwriting any owner the client sent, verified with a two-owner test on the real engine, registered as adr-security-003.

title_en: v0.3.0, bidirectional account synchronization
note_en: Local and account graphs began converging by delta with a field-level three-way merge over the domains the user selects, and account deletion started cascading into the hosted graph.

title_en: v0.3.1, the installed application updates itself
note_en: A non-blocking check at startup with a signed update bundle: the manifest is assembled in the release pipeline and a bundle that fails signature verification is refused by the client.

title_en: Web Vinc live at full write parity
note_en: The same frontend built for the browser went live, authenticated by the account session and proxied to the hub with the owner forced from the session subject, carrying every write operation the desktop has.

title_en: Copy replaced in design work, and the decks restored
note_en: Screen copy was rewritten outside the shipped decks and had to be put back, which is the origin of the rule that the English and Korean decks are the source and a mockup is a screen.

note_en: Nine structural repairs landed together, the largest being the open layer ported into the live write path so a user-authored type persists as an Entity carrier instead of being skipped, taking the store schema to version two.

title_en: The embedded driver switch cleared by three measurements

title_en: v0.5.1 shipped a sidecar that could not open the store
note_en: The interface overhaul and the driver switch shipped, and with them a regression in which the frozen sidecar opened no store at all: installation succeeded, health reported no reachable store, and every read and write failed quietly.

title_en: The deployment runbook written down as one record
note_en: Delivery was written down as a single runbook covering every surface, its trigger and its ordering, kept as a repository file rather than in the graph, an exception the new scheme has not yet settled.

title_en: Every member's synchronization pull returned nothing
note_en: The hub's pull handler read a metadata key that was never separated by owner, so every member's pull returned empty data deterministically rather than intermittently, fixed by passing the owner's real domain explicitly and hotfixed on the hub before the desktop caught up.

title_en: v0.5.3, the store failure traced and the second driver removed
note_en: The failure was a native submodule loaded by dynamic import that the freezer's static analysis could not see, fixed by collecting the whole package, after which the dual-driver rails were removed and the smoke test began actually starting the server instead of running help.
